description: Register allocation decomposed. The back-end's hardest problem. Liveness analysis, interference graph, graph coloring (Chaitin-Briggs, IRC), linear scan, LLVM's Greedy. SSA-based allocation. Spill cost models, live range splitting, coalescing.

sub_mechanisms.name: liveness_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Backward dataflow: for each program point, which variables are live (used in some future path)? Iterates to fixed point.
sub_mechanisms.why: Required input for register allocation. A variable can use a register only when live. Standard backward analysis: live_out = ∪ live_in of successors; live_in = use ∪ (live_out - def).

sub_mechanisms.name: interference_graph
sub_mechanisms.definition: Graph where nodes are values + edges connect two values simultaneously live. K-coloring assigns registers without conflicts.
sub_mechanisms.why: K colors = K physical registers. Two values that interfere need different registers. Coloring the graph with K colors solves register assignment. NP-hard in general but tractable heuristically.

sub_mechanisms.name: Chaitin_Briggs_algorithm
sub_mechanisms.definition: Repeatedly: remove low-degree (< K) nodes from graph (push on stack); pop + color avoiding neighbours. If high-degree node remains, choose to spill.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classic graph coloring RA. Simplification (push) + selection (pop + color). Optimistic coloring: assume high-degree nodes might still color. Heuristic spill choice when no K-color exists.

sub_mechanisms.name: spill_cost
sub_mechanisms.definition: Estimated cost of spilling a value: function of use count, loop nesting depth, distance to next use.
sub_mechanisms.why: Choosing which value to spill matters: spilling a hot variable hurts much more than a cold one. Cost models guide the choice. Modern allocators use loop-nesting-weighted use count.

sub_mechanisms.name: live_range_splitting
sub_mechanisms.definition: Split a live range at a strategic point (often a basic block boundary). Two halves can have different register assignments.
sub_mechanisms.why: A long live range might span high-pressure regions; splitting lets the pressure regions get registers. Pre-split, the whole range either fits or spills. Modern allocators do this extensively.

sub_mechanisms.name: coalescing
sub_mechanisms.definition: When a move instruction copies a to b, attempt to assign both to the same register, eliminating the move.
sub_mechanisms.why: Code with many move instructions (common after SSA destruction) wastes registers + executes unnecessary copies. Coalescing eliminates moves at the cost of merging live ranges (more potential interference).

sub_mechanisms.name: iterated_register_coalescing
sub_mechanisms.definition: IRC: integrate coalescing into the coloring pipeline. Coalesce conservatively, simplify, repeat.
sub_mechanisms.why: Aggressive coalescing causes spills; conservative misses optimisations. IRC's interleaved approach (Briggs-style) is the standard production technique.

sub_mechanisms.name: linear_scan_algorithm
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sort live ranges by start point. Sweep through: at each point, assign register to ranges starting; release registers of ranges ending. Spill if pool exhausted.
sub_mechanisms.why: O(n log n) vs graph coloring's NP-hard. Lower quality (~10% worse codes). Used in JITs where compile time matters. LLVM's first allocator was linear scan; replaced by Greedy.

sub_mechanisms.name: LLVM_Greedy_allocator
sub_mechanisms.definition: LLVM's current allocator. Priority-based: process live ranges by priority. Splits ranges, evicts lower-priority assignments. Iterative refinement.
sub_mechanisms.why: Quality close to graph coloring + speed close to linear scan. Default in LLVM since 2011. The priority + splitting + eviction triad lets it handle complex pressure scenarios.

sub_mechanisms.name: SSA_based_RA
sub_mechanisms.definition: Allocator that preserves SSA form throughout. Interference graphs of SSA programs are chordal — polynomial-time K-colorable.
sub_mechanisms.why: Chordal graphs have polynomial-time optimal coloring. SSA-based RA exploits this. Active research; some implementations (HotSpot's Graal) use it. Compile-time advantage for high-quality allocation.

sub_mechanisms.name: caller_callee_saved_registers
sub_mechanisms.definition: Calling convention divides registers: caller-saved (caller preserves before call), callee-saved (callee preserves on entry).
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets allocator know which registers are 'free' across calls (caller-saved) vs requiring save/restore (callee-saved). Affects spill cost analysis. Different per ABI.

sub_mechanisms.name: register_pressure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Number of simultaneously live values at a point. If > K, some values must spill.
sub_mechanisms.why: Local property predicting spills. High-pressure regions need attention from the allocator + IR generator. Spill-reload pairs are the cost.

derivation_rules.name: K_colorable_iff_no_spill_needed
if: interference graph is K-colorable (K = available registers)
derivation_rules.why: K-coloring assigns each value to one of K registers without conflicts. Spill required only when no K-coloring exists. Coloring being NP-hard means allocators sometimes spill where optimal solution wouldn't.

derivation_rules.name: SSA_interference_graphs_chordal
then: interference graph is chordal, hence optimally K-colorable in polynomial time
derivation_rules.why: Property of SSA: live ranges are tree-shaped (single definition). Resulting interference graphs are chordal. Chordal graphs have O(V+E) optimal coloring. Active research direction in JIT allocation.

derivation_rules.name: linear_scan_trades_quality_for_compile_time
derivation_rules.why: Linear scan: O(n log n) vs graph coloring's super-linear. JITs compile while user waits — fast allocation wins even at 10% code quality loss. V8, LuaJIT, .NET JITs use linear scan or variants.

derivation_rules.name: live_range_splitting_relieves_local_pressure
if: a live range spans regions of varying register pressure
then: splitting at pressure boundaries lets each segment get a register
derivation_rules.why: Without splitting, whole range either fits or spills. With splitting, low-pressure sub-ranges keep registers; high-pressure sub-ranges spill. Total spill traffic reduces.

derivation_rules.name: coalescing_eliminates_redundant_moves
if: copy instruction has non-interfering source and destination
then: coalescing merges them, eliminating the copy
derivation_rules.why: SSA destruction inserts copies; many are redundant. Coalescing identifies them. Quality matters: aggressive coalescing causes spills (merged range has more interference); conservative misses opportunities.
